The indemnified party shall promptly notify the indemnifying party in writing of any claim for which indemnification is sought, cooperate reasonably at the indemnifying party's cost, and take commercially reasonable steps to mitigate its Losses. The indemnifying party shall have reasonable control of the defense and settlement of any such claim, provided that no settlement imposing any obligation or liability on the indemnified party shall be made without its prior written consent.

Prior to initiating arbitration, the parties shall attempt to resolve any dispute through good-faith senior executive negotiation for thirty (30) days following written notice of the dispute. Any unresolved controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement or the breach thereof shall be settled by binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association ("AAA") under its Commercial Arbitration Rules and the Federal Arbitration Act, and judgment on the award rendered by the arbitrator shall be binding and may be entered in any court having jurisdiction thereof. resolved_entries.suggested_fix_before_reconciliation: Change Orders. Any change in the details of a Work Order or the assumptions upon which the Work Order is based (including, but not limited to, changes in an agreed starting date for a Project or suspension of the Project by Sponsor) may require changes in the budget and/or timelines, and shall require a written amendment to the Work Order (a "Change Order"). Each Change Order shall detail the requested changes to the applicable task, responsibility, duty, budget, timeline or other matter. The Change Order will become effective upon the execution of the Change Order by duly authorized representatives of both parties, and the parties will agree upon a reasonable period of time within which Quintiles shall implement the changes. Both parties agree to act in good faith and promptly when considering a Change Order requested by the other party. Without limiting the foregoing, Sponsor agrees that it will not unreasonably withhold approval of a Change Order, if the proposed changes in budgets or timelines result from, among other appropriate reasons, forces outside the reasonable control of Quintiles or Sponsor's changes in the assumptions upon which the initial budget or timelines were based, including, but not limited to, the assumptions set forth in the budget or timelines. Quintiles reserves the right to postpone effecting material changes in the Project's scope until such time as the parties agree to and execute the corresponding Change Order. For any Change Order that affects the scope of the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles, Quintiles and Sponsor shall execute a corresponding amendment to the Transfer of Obligations Form. Sponsor shall file such amendment where appropriate, or as required by law or regulation. No amendment or modification of this Agreement, any Work Order, or any schedule or exhibit hereto shall be effective unless set forth in a writing executed by duly authorized representatives of both parties, and no oral agreement, course of conduct, or course of dealing shall constitute or be deemed to modify any provision of this Agreement or any Work Order.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Master Services Agreement (“Agreement”) is made between Sunesis Pharmaceuticals, Inc. which has a place of business at 341 Oyster Point Boulevard, South San Francisco, California 94080 (hereinafter “Sponsor”), and Quintiles, Inc. a North Carolina corporation having a place of business at 10245 Hickman Mills Drive, Kansas City, MO 64137 (hereinafter “Quintiles”). When signed by both parties, this Agreement will set forth the terms and conditions under which Quintiles agrees to provide certain services to Sponsor as set forth herein.

Recitals:

Sponsor is in the business of drug discovery, research and development for various pharmaceutical products. Quintiles is in the business of providing drug development and manufacturing services, clinical trial services, and other services for the pharmaceutical, medical device and biotechnology industries.

Sponsor and Quintiles desire to enter into this Agreement to provide the terms and conditions upon which Sponsor may engage Quintiles from time-to-time to provide services for individual studies or projects by executing individual Work Orders (as defined below) specifying the details of the services and the related terms and conditions.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Scope of the Agreement; Work Orders; Nature of Services; Transfer of Obligations.

Scope of Agreement. As a “master” form of contract, this Agreement allows the parties to contract for multiple projects through the issuance of multiple Work Orders (as discussed in Section 1.2 below), without having to re-negotiate the basic terms and conditions contained herein. This Agreement covers the provision of services by Quintiles and Quintiles’ corporate affiliates (see Section 16.1) and, accordingly, this Agreement represents a vehicle by which Sponsor can efficiently contract with Quintiles and its corporate affiliates for a broad range of specific services.

Work Orders. The specific details of each project under this Agreement (each “Project”) shall be separately negotiated and specified in writing on terms and in a form acceptable to the parties (each such writing, a “Work Order”). A sample Work Order is attached hereto as Exhibit A. Each Work Order will include, without limitations, the scope of work, timeline(s), and budget and payment schedule. Each Work Order shall be subject to all of the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including (when applicable) the terms and conditions set forth in the quality requirement agreement to be completed by the parties which will be made part of and attached to this Agreement (the “Quality Agreement”), in addition to the specific details set forth in the Work Order.

Integration; Precedence. Any Work Order or Change Order (as defined in Section 4.0 below) and other exhibits issued and executed pursuant to this Agreement will be made part hereof and incorporated herein by reference. To the extent any terms or provisions of a Work Order or Change Order conflict with the terms and provisions of this Agreement, the terms and provisions of this Agreement shall control, except to the extent that the applicable Work Order or Change Order expressly and specifically states an intent to supersede the Agreement on a specific matter.

Nature of Services. The services covered by this Agreement may include expert consultation, clinical trial services, statistical programming and analysis, clerical, project management, central laboratory services, preclinical services, pharmaceutical sciences services, and related data processing, data management and regulatory services, and other research and development services requested by Sponsor and agreed to by Quintiles as set forth in the relevant Work Order (collectively, the “Services”).

Transfer of Obligations. Quintiles and Sponsor, where appropriate, shall cooperate in the completion of a Transfer of Obligations Form in conjunction with the relevant Work Order. Any responsibilities not specifically transferred in the Transfer of Obligations Form shall remain the regulatory responsibility of Sponsor. The Transfer of Obligations Form will be filed with the Food and Drug Administration (“FDA”) by Sponsor where appropriate, or as required by law or regulation.

explanation_call.reason: The clause omits several market-standard payment terms that create material risk for both parties: it does not specify how fees are calculated (e.g., fixed, time-and-materials, or milestone-based), does not address whether and how fees may be modified during the term, and contains no consequence for late payment, leaving Quintiles without a remedy for overdue undisputed amounts. The dispute resolution mechanism uses "as soon as practicable" with no defined deadline, which is unenforceable in practice and may allow indefinite deferral of resolution. These gaps expose Quintiles to cash-flow uncertainty and Sponsor to uncontrolled fee variation, and the absence of a formal dispute notice period undermines the payment waterfall that the clause otherwise tries to establish.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Payment of Fees and Expenses. Sponsor will pay Quintiles for fees, expenses and pass-through costs in accordance with the fee structure (whether fixed, time-and-materials, or milestone-based, as specified therein), budget, and payment schedule contained in each Work Order. Fees may only be modified by a written amendment to the applicable Work Order signed by both parties. Sponsor agrees that the budget and payment schedule for each Work Order will be structured in an effort to maintain cash neutrality for Quintiles (with respect to professional fees, pass-through costs and otherwise). Unless otherwise agreed in a particular Work Order, the following shall apply: (a) Quintiles will invoice Sponsor monthly for fees, expenses and pass-through costs incurred in performing the Services; and (b) Sponsor shall pay each invoice within thirty (30) days of receipt. Undisputed amounts not paid by the due date shall accrue interest at one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, whichever is lower. If any portion of an invoice is disputed, Sponsor shall pay the undisputed amounts as provided above and the parties shall use good faith efforts to reconcile the disputed amount within thirty (30) days following written notice of dispute.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text: Payment of Fees and Expenses. Sponsor will pay Quintiles for fees, expenses and pass-through costs in accordance with the budget and payment schedule contained in each Work Order. Sponsor agrees that the budget and payment schedule for each Work Order will be structured in an effort to maintain cash neutrality for Quintiles (with respect to the payment of professional fees, pass-through costs and otherwise). Unless otherwise agreed in a particular Work Order, the following shall apply: (a) Quintiles will invoice Sponsor monthly for the fees, expenses and pass-through costs incurred in performing the Services; and, (b) Sponsor shall pay each invoice within thirty (30) days of receipt of the invoice. If any portion of an invoice is disputed, then Sponsor shall pay the undisputed amounts as set forth in the preceding sentence and the parties shall use good faith efforts to reconcile the disputed amount as soon as practicable.

explanation_call.reason: The Term clause establishes a five-year duration but does no more than cross-reference Section 15 for all termination mechanics, leaving the clause commercially incomplete. Neither party has visibility within this provision as to whether termination for convenience is available, what notice period applies, that termination must be effected by written notice, or when termination takes effect — creating material uncertainty about exit rights for both parties. This gap is particularly significant for a five-year commitment, where either party may need to terminate for convenience and the absence of a minimum notice period creates operational and planning risk. The cure period, consequences of termination, survival, and transition arrangements should be addressed in Section 15; however, the foundational termination-for-convenience right and written notice mechanics belong in the Term clause itself.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Term. This Agreement shall commence on the date it has been signed by all parties and shall continue for a period of five (5) years from the date of execution, unless earlier terminated: (a) by either party for cause in accordance with Section 15 below; or (b) by either party for convenience upon not less than ninety (90) days' prior written notice to the other party, such termination taking effect upon expiry of that notice period.

explanation_call.reason: The clause establishes a Change Order process for Work Order amendments but contains three material gaps that create enforceability and operational risk for both parties. First, execution is required by "both parties" without specifying that signatories must be duly authorized representatives, which leaves room for disputes over whether a Change Order executed by an unauthorized individual is binding. Second, the amendment mechanism is confined to Work Orders, leaving changes to the broader Agreement, schedules, and exhibits outside any formal amendment framework. Third, the clause contains no anti-oral-modification or no-waiver-by-conduct provision, meaning either party could argue that informal communications or conduct altered their obligations, undermining the written Change Order requirement entirely.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Change Orders. Any change in the details of a Work Order or the assumptions upon which the Work Order is based (including, but not limited to, changes in an agreed starting date for a Project or suspension of the Project by Sponsor) may require changes in the budget and/or timelines, and shall require a written amendment to the Work Order (a "Change Order"). Each Change Order shall detail the requested changes to the applicable task, responsibility, duty, budget, timeline or other matter. The Change Order will become effective upon the execution of the Change Order by duly authorized representatives of both parties, and the parties will agree upon a reasonable period of time within which Quintiles shall implement the changes. Both parties agree to act in good faith and promptly when considering a Change Order requested by the other party. Without limiting the foregoing, Sponsor agrees that it will not unreasonably withhold approval of a Change Order, if the proposed changes in budgets or timelines result from, among other appropriate reasons, forces outside the reasonable control of Quintiles or Sponsor's changes in the assumptions upon which the initial budget or timelines were based, including, but not limited to, the assumptions set forth in the budget or timelines. Quintiles reserves the right to postpone effecting material changes in the Project's scope until such time as the parties agree to and execute the corresponding Change Order. For any Change Order that affects the scope of the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles, Quintiles and Sponsor shall execute a corresponding amendment to the Transfer of Obligations Form. Sponsor shall file such amendment where appropriate, or as required by law or regulation. No amendment or modification of this Agreement, any Work Order, or any schedule or exhibit hereto shall be effective unless set forth in a writing executed by duly authorized representatives of both parties, and no oral agreement, course of conduct, or course of dealing shall constitute or be deemed to modify any provision of this Agreement or any Work Order.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Confidentiality.

Sponsor Confidential Information. It is understood that during the course of this Agreement, Quintiles and its employees may be exposed to data and information that are confidential and proprietary to Sponsor. All such data and information (hereinafter “Sponsor Confidential Information”) written or verbal, tangible or intangible, made available, disclosed, or otherwise made known to Quintiles and its employees as a result of Services under this Agreement shall be considered confidential and shall be considered the sole property of Sponsor.

Quintiles Confidential Information. All information regarding Quintiles’ operations, methods, and pricing and all Quintiles’ Property (as defined in Section 6.2 below), disclosed by Quintiles to Sponsor in connection with this Agreement is proprietary, confidential information belonging to Quintiles (the “Quintiles Confidential Information”).

Confidentiality Obligations. For the purposes of Sections 5.3 and 5.4, Confidential Information shall mean both Sponsor Confidential Information and Quintiles Confidential Information. Each party hereunder agrees that Confidential Information disclosed by one party to the other shall be clearly marked ‘confidential’, or if disclosed orally, is confirmed in writing as having been disclosed as confidential or proprietary of the disclosing party within thirty (30) days after such disclosure. Quintiles and Sponsor each agree that it will only provide Confidential Information to the other party on a need-to-know basis and to the extent that Confidential Information is required for its undertaking of this Agreement. The Confidential Information shall be used by the receiving party and its employees only for purposes of performing the receiving party’s obligations hereunder. Except as otherwise expressly authorized in this Agreement, each party agrees that it will not make copies or duplicates of any Confidential Information, or reveal, publish or otherwise disclose the Confidential Information of the other party to any third party without the prior written consent of the disclosing party. Each party agrees that it will not disclose the terms of this Agreement or any Work Order to any third party without the written consent of the other party, which shall not unreasonably be withheld. These obligations of confidentiality and nondisclosure shall remain in effect for a period often (10) years after the completion or termination of the applicable Work Order.

The foregoing obligations shall not apply to Confidential Information to the extent that it: (a) is or becomes generally available to the public other than as a result of a disclosure by the receiving party; (b) becomes available to the receiving party on a non-confidential basis from a source which is not prohibited from disclosing such information; (c) was developed independently of any disclosure by the disclosing party or was known to the receiving party prior to its receipt from the disclosing party, as shown by receiving party’s contemporaneous written evidence; or, (d) is required by law or regulation to be disclosed, provided that the receiving party shall provide prompt notice of such requirement to the disclosing party to enable the disclosing party to seek a protective order or otherwise prevent or restrict such disclosure.

- Limit on use: "The Confidential Information shall be used by the receiving party and its employees only for purposes of performing the receiving party's obligations hereunder" - YES
- Both stated → MET

explanation_call.reason: The clause defines Sponsor's Property and establishes Sponsor's ownership but is silent on what happens if any element of Sponsor's Property infringes a third party's intellectual property rights. This omission leaves Quintiles exposed to unallocated risk when using materials supplied by Sponsor, while Sponsor has no contractual obligation to warrant the legitimacy of what it supplies. A market-standard ownership clause should include a representation that the supplying party's materials do not infringe third-party intellectual property rights so that responsibility for any resulting claims is clearly allocated at the point of supply.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Sponsor's Property. Sponsor's property shall mean any invention, trade secret or know-how related to or derived from any materials, documents, programs or information belonging to Sponsor and supplied to Quintiles pursuant to this Agreement, and such inventions, trade secret and know-how shall remain the exclusive property of Sponsor (collectively "Sponsor's Property"). Sponsor represents and warrants that Sponsor's Property does not infringe any third-party intellectual property rights.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Ownership and Inventions; No Implied Rights.

Sponsor’s Property. Sponsor’s property shall mean any invention, trade secret or know-how related to or derived from any materials, documents, programs or information belonging to Sponsor and supplied to Quintiles pursuant to this Agreement, and such inventions, trade secret and know-how shall remain the exclusive property of Sponsor (collectively “Sponsor’s Property”).

Quintiles’ Property. Any inventions, processes, know-how, trade secrets, improvements, other intellectual properties and other assets, including but not limited to analytical methods, procedures and techniques, procedure manuals, personnel data, financial information, computer technical expertise and software, which have been developed by Quintiles independent of this Agreement, which relates to Quintiles’ business or operations, and not falling within Section 6.3a below, shall remain the exclusive property of Quintiles (collectively “Quintiles’ Property”). For the avoidance of doubt, Quintiles’ Property shall not include any inventions, trade secrets or know-how that incorporates data, information or know-how derived from Sponsor’s Property of Sponsor Confidential Information.

Project Intellectual Property (IP).

Any inventions and discoveries, including any data and information generated or derived by Quintiles as the result of Services performed by Quintiles under this Agreement and/or uses Sponsor Confidential Information (collectively “Project IP”) are the sole and exclusive property of Sponsor and Quintiles hereby assigns to Sponsor any Quintiles rights to Project IP (including any patent and all other intellectual property rights therein). Project IP shall be deemed Sponsor Confidential Information for purposes of Section 5.1 above.

Sponsor and Quintiles agree that any Quintiles’ Property or improvements thereto which are used, improved, modified or developed by Quintiles under the term of this Agreement, and which do not use or include any Sponsor Confidential Information or Sponsor’s Property, are the sole and exclusive property of Quintiles and shall be deemed Quintiles Confidential Information. To the extent the Quintiles Software (defined as programs for the purposes of data derivations, population identification, production of statistical analysis outputs, is determined to be necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data generated as a result of the Services performed by Quintiles under this Agreement, Quintiles grants to Sponsor a royalty-free, non-exclusive license with the right use by only Sponsor (and not its Affiliates or other third parties) without the right to sell, assign or sublicense such software programs and any improvements thereto in connection with such Sponsor project under the Agreement. For such software, Quintiles will provide to Sponsor the macros. When Quintiles’ Software is no longer necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data as described above, such Quintiles Software shall be returned to Quintiles.

No Implied Rights. Except as expressly provided herein, neither party shall have any right, title or interest to or in any patents, patent applications, know-how (whether patentable or not) or other intellectual property rights of the other party.

Let me analyze this IP clause carefully against each criterion.

**IPR-01: Who owns each kind of IP (pre-existing IP, newly created IP, data)?**
- Pre-existing IP: Sponsor's Property (§78D28658) - Sponsor keeps theirs; Quintiles' Property (§8A6387BA) - Quintiles keeps theirs. Met.
- Newly created IP (Project IP): §634D7DC9 assigns to Sponsor. Met.
- Data: §634D7DC9 mentions "data and information generated or derived by Quintiles as the result of Services" - this is Project IP owned by Sponsor. 
All three categories addressed. Met.

**IPR-02: Each party keeps its pre-existing IP?**
Sponsor's property remains exclusive under §78D28658, and Quintiles' property remains exclusive under §8A6387BA. Met.

**IPR-03: Licence granted with scope stated?**
§80E5920E grants Sponsor a royalty-free, non-exclusive license limited to Sponsor only (excluding Affiliates or third parties), without rights to sell, assign, or sublicense.

I note the license's purpose is to access and use study data, with duration tied to project need (software returned when no longer necessary), non-exclusive terms, and clear scope limitations. Met.

**IPR-04: Assignment that takes effect (not a promise to assign)?**
§634D7DC9 uses "hereby assigns" language, which is a present-tense assignment taking effect immediately rather than a future promise. Met.

**IPR-05: Limits on how each party may use the other's IP?**
§67DE8F74 restricts each party from claiming rights to the other's patents, know-how, or IP except as expressly provided, while §80E5920E's licence terms reinforce these limits by prohibiting sale, assignment, or sublicensing and restricting use to Sponsor alone.

For Quintiles' use of Sponsor's IP, §8A6387BA excludes anything derived from Sponsor's Property from Quintiles' Property, and §634D7DC9 assigns Project IP built on Sponsor Confidential Information to Sponsor. Combined with §67DE8F74's general no-implied-rights clause, this covers both directions adequately. Met.

**IPR-06: Third-party IP infringement claims?**
Checking the clause text, there's no mention of indemnification or responsibility for third-party infringement claims—§67DE8F74's "No Implied Rights" provision doesn't touch on this either. Not met - not stated in text.

**IPR-07: Background vs foreground IP distinction?**
The agreement clearly separates background IP (Sponsor's Property under §78D28658 and Quintiles' Property under §8A6387BA) from foreground IP (Project IP under §634D7DC9 and improvements under §80E5920E), with ownership allocated for both. Met.

**IPR-08: Broad rights for provider to use customer data?**
Nothing grants Quintiles rights to use Sponsor's data for its own product development—§634D7DC9 assigns Project IP (including derived data) to Sponsor, and §8A6387BA explicitly excludes anything incorporating Sponsor's data or confidential information from Quintiles' Property. Met.

explanation_call.reason: The clause addresses record retention and disposition of Sponsor's materials but is entirely silent on audit rights, leaving neither party with a defined mechanism to verify compliance with record-keeping, data security, or performance obligations under the Agreement. The absence of audit frequency, advance notice requirements, cooperation obligations, remediation duties, and cost allocation creates material uncertainty and renders any audit right unenforceable in practice. For a master services agreement in a regulated environment—particularly one involving FDA record-keeping obligations expressly referenced in the clause—the lack of audit mechanics is a significant operational and compliance gap for both parties. Any audit right added should be considered in conjunction with the confidentiality provisions referenced elsewhere in the Agreement to ensure that access does not constitute an unauthorized disclosure of Quintiles' proprietary information.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Records and Materials. Quintiles agrees to retain all records and data generated in the performance of any Project under this Agreement, and other Project-related materials including without limitation Sponsor's proprietary compound ("Records and Materials"), and further agrees to maintain all Records and Materials in a secure area reasonably protected from fire, theft and destruction. Sponsor shall have the right, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice and no more than once per calendar year absent cause, to audit Quintiles' relevant records, systems, and premises in connection with the Services; Quintiles shall cooperate with any such audit, provide reasonable access to relevant records and personnel, and promptly remediate any material findings identified, with audit costs borne by Sponsor unless material non-compliance by Quintiles is identified, in which case Quintiles shall bear such costs. At the completion of the Services by Quintiles, all materials, information and all other data owned by Sponsor, regardless of the method of storage or retrieval, shall be delivered to Sponsor in such form as is then currently in the possession of Quintiles, subject to the payment obligations set forth in Section 2 herein. Alternatively, at Sponsor's option and written request, such materials and data may be (i) retained by Quintiles for Sponsor for an agreed-upon time period, or (ii) disposed of pursuant to the written directions of Sponsor. Sponsor shall pay the costs associated with any of the above options and shall pay a to-be-determined fee for storage by Quintiles of records and materials after completion or termination of the Services. Quintiles, however, reserves the right to retain, at its own cost and subject to the confidentiality provisions herein, copies of all materials that may be needed to satisfy regulatory requirements or to resolve disputes regarding the Services. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to transfer from Sponsor to Quintiles any FDA or regulatory record-keeping requirements unless such transfer is specifically provided for in the applicable Transfer of Obligations Form.

explanation_call.reason: The clause correctly disclaims a partnership, agency, and employment relationship but omits two market-standard elements that reinforce the independent contractor characterization: an allocation of control over the manner and means of performance, and each party's responsibility for its own personnel's compensation, taxes, and benefits. Without these elements, the clause provides only a label rather than the substantive indicia that courts and tax authorities look to when assessing whether a relationship is genuinely independent, exposing both parties to potential employment misclassification liability and related tax obligations. Including these elements is a standard bilateral protection in a Master Services Agreement and does not favor either party.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Independent Contractor Relationship. For the purposes of this Agreement, the parties hereto are independent contractors, each retaining control over the manner and means of its own performance, and nothing contained in this Agreement shall be construed to place them in the relationship of partners, principal and agent, employer/employee or joint venturers. Each party is solely responsible for the compensation, taxes, and benefits of its own personnel. Neither party shall have the power or right to bind or obligate the other party, and neither party shall hold itself out as having such authority.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Regulatory Compliance; Certification; Inspections.

Quintiles agrees that its Services will be conducted in compliance with all applicable laws, rules and regulations, including but not limited to the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act and the regulations promulgated pursuant thereto, and with the standard of care customary in the contract research organization industry. Regarding the FDA’s electronic records and signatures regulation, 21 CFR Part 11 (“Part 11”), Quintiles has a compliance plan in place as to its applicable database applications and electronic records systems and it is working diligently to implement its plan. Quintiles, however, is not responsible for the compliance or non-compliance of applications or systems used by third parties (including, but not limited to, investigative sites or third party laboratories), or any Part 11 audits or assessments thereof, unless such applications or systems are owned by Quintiles. Quintiles’ standard operating procedures will be used in performance of the Services, unless otherwise specifically stated in the Work Order. Sponsor represents that it will cooperate with Quintiles in taking any actions that Quintiles and Sponsor reasonably believes are necessary to comply with the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles hereunder.

Quintiles certifies that it has not been debarred under the Generic Drug Enforcement Act and that it will not knowingly employ any person or entity that has been so debarred to perform any Services under this Agreement. Sponsor represents and certifies that it will not require Quintiles to perform any assignments or tasks in a manner that would violate any applicable law or regulation.

During the term of this Agreement, Quintiles will permit Sponsor’s representatives (unless such representatives are competitors of Quintiles) to examine or audit the work performed hereunder and the facilities at which the work is conducted upon reasonable advance notice during regular business hours to determine that the Project assignment is being conducted in accordance with the relevant Work Order and that the facilities are adequate. Quintiles shall cooperate with Sponsor and allow Sponsor access to relevant records and data to the extent permitted by law. All information (other than Sponsor Confidential Information) disclosed, revealed to or ascertained by Sponsor in connection with any such audit or examination or in connection with any correspondence between Quintiles and any regulatory authorities (including any FDA Form 483 notices) shall be deemed to constitute Quintiles Confidential Information for purposes of this Agreement. Sponsor shall reimburse Quintiles for its time and reasonable expenses associated with any such audit by Sponsor, unless such audit finds that Quintiles breached this Agreement or any applicable law or regulation.

If any governmental or regulatory agency conducts, or gives notice to Quintiles of its intent to conduct an inspection or to take any regulatory action with respect to any Project or Services pursuant to this Agreement, Quintiles will promptly notify Sponsor prior to complying with such request. Where reasonably practicable, Sponsor will be given the opportunity to have a representative present during any governmental or regulatory inspection. Sponsor shall reimburse Quintiles for its time and reasonable expenses (including reasonable attorney fees and the costs of responding to findings) associated with any such inspection, unless such inspection finds that Quintiles breached this Agreement or any applicable law or regulation.

suggestions.reason: The clause imposes compliance obligations on Quintiles with respect to general applicable laws and FDA regulations but omits three market-standard compliance requirements that expose both parties to legal and reputational risk: there is no reference to anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws, no obligation on either party to notify the other of a material compliance breach affecting the Agreement, and no acknowledgment of supply-chain obligations regarding forced labour, child labour, or human trafficking. The absence of a mutual breach-notification obligation is particularly significant in a clinical research context, where a regulatory violation by either party could directly affect study integrity, regulatory submissions, and the other party's own legal exposure. Additionally, while Quintiles' standard operating procedures are referenced, there is no mechanism for Sponsor to access or review them, limiting Sponsor's ability to assess compliance standards prior to or during performance.
suggestions.original_text: Quintiles agrees that its Services will be conducted in compliance with all applicable laws, rules and regulations, including but not limited to the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act and the regulations promulgated pursuant thereto, and with the standard of care customary in the contract research organization industry. Regarding the FDA’s electronic records and signatures regulation, 21 CFR Part 11 (“Part 11”), Quintiles has a compliance plan in place as to its applicable database applications and electronic records systems and it is working diligently to implement its plan. Quintiles, however, is not responsible for the compliance or non-compliance of applications or systems used by third parties (including, but not limited to, investigative sites or third party laboratories), or any Part 11 audits or assessments thereof, unless such applications or systems are owned by Quintiles. Quintiles’ standard operating procedures will be used in performance of the Services, unless otherwise specifically stated in the Work Order. Sponsor represents that it will cooperate with Quintiles in taking any actions that Quintiles and Sponsor reasonably believes are necessary to comply with the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles hereunder.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Quintiles agrees that its Services will be conducted in compliance with all applicable laws, rules and regulations, including but not limited to the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act and the regulations promulgated pursuant thereto, applicable anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws, and applicable laws prohibiting forced labour, child labour, and human trafficking in its supply chain, and with the standard of care customary in the contract research organization industry. Regarding the FDA's electronic records and signatures regulation, 21 CFR Part 11 ("Part 11"), Quintiles has a compliance plan in place as to its applicable database applications and electronic records systems and it is working diligently to implement its plan. Quintiles, however, is not responsible for the compliance or non-compliance of applications or systems used by third parties (including, but not limited to, investigative sites or third party laboratories), or any Part 11 audits or assessments thereof, unless such applications or systems are owned by Quintiles. Quintiles' standard operating procedures will be used in performance of the Services, unless otherwise specifically stated in the Work Order, and shall be made available to Sponsor for review upon written request. Sponsor represents that it will cooperate with Quintiles in taking any actions that Quintiles and Sponsor reasonably believe are necessary to comply with the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles hereunder. Each party shall promptly notify the other in writing upon becoming aware of any material breach of applicable law or regulation that affects the performance or subject matter of this Agreement.

Additionally, the phrase "in any way prevent" sets an imprecisely broad standard that could capture incidental or remote impediments that do not practically affect service delivery, creating enforcement uncertainty and potential exposure for Quintiles beyond what the parties would commercially intend. The mutual representation gap and the vague operative threshold together undermine both the balance and the legal clarity of the provision.

Let me evaluate this clause against each criterion.

The clause is a "Conflict of Agreements" clause in a Master Services Agreement. It contains:
1. A representation by Quintiles that it is not currently a party to any agreement preventing it from fulfilling its obligations.
2. An agreement by Quintiles not to enter into any agreement during the term that would prevent it from providing the Services.

Let me evaluate each criterion:

**GEN-01: One-sided obligations**
The clause is entirely one-sided - only Quintiles (the Service Provider) makes representations and undertakes obligations. The Sponsor makes no reciprocal representation or undertaking. However, in the context of a conflict of agreements clause, this is commercially reasonable because it's the service provider who would typically have conflicts of interest/obligations that could prevent performance. The Sponsor's obligations wouldn't create a conflict with the service provider's ability to deliver. So this is partly met - the obligation is one-sided but it's somewhat commercially justified given the nature of the clause.
Still, one could argue the Sponsor might also have conflicting exclusivity arrangements or commitments affecting its payment/cooperation duties, so a fully neutral drafting might include a reciprocal representation from the Sponsor too. On balance I'll lean toward "Met" since the asymmetry reflects a provider-specific concern about service delivery capability rather than unfair drafting.

Moving through the remaining checklist: no vague time standards beyond the defined term, no financial amounts or caps present, no problematic undefined terms, no unfilled placeholders, and no internal contradictions in this clause.

For rights without obligations, the clause only imposes duties on Quintiles with no explicit reciprocal right stated here, but since the broader MSA presumably provides consideration elsewhere, I'll mark this "Met" based on the overall agreement structure.

Looking at ambiguity, the phrase "in any way prevent" is fairly broad and could sweep in partial hindrances rather than just outright prevention, so I'll call this "Partly met." The conditions and triggers, though, are clear - the covenant runs during the term, the representation applies as of the agreement date - so that one's "Met."

Now I'm walking through the remaining checks: GEN-01 is one-sided since only Quintiles makes representations, but that asymmetry seems commercially justified given the clause concerns the provider's ability to perform, so "Partly met." GEN-02 through GEN-07 look clean - no vague standards, no financial amounts at play, terms are either defined or carry plain commercial meaning, no indemnity exposure, no placeholders, and nothing contradictory.

explanation_thinking_by_para.A185D98A:
Let me analyze the issues identified:

1. The clause is one-sided - only Quintiles makes representations and undertakings; Sponsor makes no corresponding representation that it is not party to any agreement that would prevent it from fulfilling its obligations under this Agreement.

2. The obligation is unilateral - only Quintiles is restricted from entering into conflicting agreements during the term.

3. The phrase "would in any way prevent it from providing the Services" is ambiguous - "in any way" is overly broad and could capture indirect or tangential impediments that don't practically affect service delivery.

The fix should:
1. Add a reciprocal representation from Sponsor that it is not party to any agreement that would prevent it from fulfilling its obligations under this Agreement.
2. Replace the "in any way prevent" language with "materially prevent" to tighten the standard and avoid overbreadth.

I'm drafting revised language that makes the representation mutual between both parties while keeping Quintiles' forward-looking covenant not to take on conflicting work, now bounded by a materiality threshold rather than "any way."

I check the word count against the original to confirm it stays within range, then weigh whether Sponsor should also carry a forward-looking covenant, concluding that's not market-standard - the mutual representation plus Quintiles-specific covenant is the more natural, commercially sensible structure.

suggestions.reason: The clause imposes both a present-state representation and a forward-looking covenant exclusively on Quintiles, with no corresponding representation from Sponsor that it is not party to any agreement that would prevent it from performing its own obligations under this Agreement; this asymmetry is commercially unjustified in a bilateral master services arrangement where both parties assume material obligations. Additionally, the phrase "in any way prevent" sets an imprecisely broad standard that could capture incidental or remote impediments that do not practically affect service delivery, creating enforcement uncertainty and potential exposure for Quintiles beyond what the parties would commercially intend. The mutual representation gap and the vague operative threshold together undermine both the balance and the legal clarity of the provision.

This creates a structurally imbalanced provision: Sponsor bears full uncapped exposure for consequential and indirect losses while Quintiles and its group are comprehensively shielded. Both provisions should be extended bilaterally, with the aggregate cap anchored to the same fee-based measure, which functions as a reasonable and proportionate proxy for both parties' exposure under a given assignment or Work Order.

Neither Quintiles, nor its affiliates, nor any of Quintiles’ or its affiliate’s directors, officers, employees, subcontractors or agents shall have any liability of any type (including, but not limited to, contract, negligence, and tort liability), for any loss of profits, opportunity or goodwill, or any type of special, incidental, indirect or consequential damage or loss in connection with or arising out of this Agreement, any Work Order, or the Services performed by Quintiles hereunder. In addition, in no event shall the collective, aggregate liability (including, but not limited to, contract, negligence and tort liability) of Quintiles or its affiliates, or Quintiles’ or its affiliates’ directors, officers, employees, subcontractors and agents, under this Agreement or any Work Order hereunder exceed the amount of fees actually received by Quintiles from Sponsor for the assignment or task from which such liability arose.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, both the consequential loss exclusion and the aggregate liability cap apply exclusively to Quintiles and its affiliated personnel, with no corresponding protection extended to Sponsor. This creates a structurally imbalanced provision: Sponsor bears full uncapped exposure for consequential and indirect losses while Quintiles and its group are comprehensively shielded. Market-standard limitation of liability clauses in Master Services Agreements apply mutual caps and exclusions to both contracting parties, and a court or arbitral tribunal reviewing this clause would likely note its one-sided character, which may also affect its enforceability in certain jurisdictions. Both provisions should be extended bilaterally, with the aggregate cap anchored to the same fee-based measure, which functions as a reasonable and proportionate proxy for both parties' exposure under a given assignment or Work Order.

suggestions.reason: The warranty disclaimer, as drafted, contains no carve-out preserving either party's liability for fraud, death, or personal injury caused by negligence — categories that many jurisdictions treat as incapable of contractual exclusion, rendering any blanket limitation in those respects void and creating enforceability risk for the entire provision. The clause is also silent on whether the limitation framework applies to data breach, confidentiality breach, intellectual property infringement, or indemnification obligations, which are typically the highest-value exposure categories in a Master Services Agreement and are frequently carved out or separately addressed in market-standard drafting. Without that clarity, the scope of the disclaimer is genuinely ambiguous and open to dispute. These omissions are material cross-references to the indemnification and confidentiality provisions elsewhere in the Agreement, which may otherwise be inadvertently read as subject to this disclaimer.

Quintiles shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Sponsor, its affiliates and their respective directors, officers, employees and agents (each, a "Sponsor Indemnified Party") from and against any Losses resulting or arising from any third-party claims relating to or arising from the negligence or intentional misconduct of a Quintiles Indemnified Party. The indemnification obligations set forth in this Section are not subject to any limitation of liability provisions set forth in this Agreement. The indemnified party shall promptly notify the indemnifying party in writing of any claim for which indemnification is sought, cooperate reasonably at the indemnifying party's cost, and take commercially reasonable steps to mitigate its Losses. The indemnifying party shall have reasonable control of the defense and settlement of any such claim, provided that no settlement imposing any obligation or liability on the indemnified party shall be made without its prior written consent.

thinking_trace.extraction_thinking:
Let me analyze the indemnification clause carefully against each criterion.

The clause has two parts:
1. Sponsor indemnifies Quintiles and its affiliates, directors, officers, employees, agents ("Quintiles Indemnified Party") from any and all losses, damages, liabilities, reasonable attorney fees, court costs, and expenses ("Losses") arising from third-party claims relating to this Agreement, any Work Order, or the Services, EXCEPT to the extent Losses resulted solely from negligence or intentional misconduct of a Quintiles Indemnified Party.

2. Quintiles indemnifies Sponsor, its affiliates and their respective directors, officers, employees and agents from Losses arising from the negligence or intentional misconduct of a Quintiles Indemnified Party.
 
Checking IND-01, both indemnities specify clear triggers — Sponsor's covers third-party claims relating to the Agreement/Work Orders/Services, while Quintiles' covers negligence or intentional misconduct by a Quintiles Indemnified Party. This criterion is met.

For IND-02, it's clear which party indemnifies which: Sponsor covers Quintiles Indemnified Parties, and Quintiles covers Sponsor and its affiliates/directors/officers/employees/agents. Met.

For IND-03, both indemnities reference "Losses," a defined term covering multiple categories (damages, liabilities, attorney fees, court costs, expenses), so this is also met. Now I'm checking IND-04 — whether the indemnities are mutual or limited to matters within each party's control, noting Sponsor's indemnity is broad but carves out an exception for Quintiles' own negligence or misconduct.

Reconsidering: Quintiles' indemnity is narrow, tied strictly to its own negligence or intentional misconduct, while Sponsor's obligation is much more sweeping, covering essentially all third-party claims arising from the agreement or services regardless of fault, only excluding losses solely caused by Quintiles' negligence or misconduct — so the indemnities aren't mutual and Sponsor bears a disproportionately broader burden.

For IND-05, the clause does mention "defend" within Sponsor's indemnity language, which implies a defence obligation exists, but it doesn't clearly spell out requirements like prompt notice, control of defence, or cooperation duties.

For IND-06, since the clause is silent on how it relates to any liability cap, and I lack visibility into whether the broader agreement includes a separate limitation of liability provision, I need to flag this as ambiguous rather than definitively met or unmet.

For IND-07, there's no mitigation obligation requiring the indemnified party to take reasonable steps to limit its loss, so that's NOT MET.

Provisions that by their nature are intended to survive termination shall survive expiry or termination of this Agreement.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Termination.

Sponsor may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order without cause at any time during the term of the Agreement on thirty (30) day’s prior written notice to Quintiles.

Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order for material breach upon thirty (30) days’ written notice specifying the nature of the breach, if such breach has not been substantially cured within the thirty (30) day period. During the 30-day cure period for termination due to breach, each party will continue to perform its obligations under the Agreement. If the cure period has expired without a substantial cure of the breach, then the parties shall promptly meet to prepare a close-out schedule, and Quintiles shall cease performing all work not necessary for the orderly close-out of the Services or required by laws or regulations.

Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Work Orders immediately upon provision of written notice if the other party becomes insolvent or files for bankruptcy. Any written termination notice shall identify the specific Work Order or Work Orders that are being terminated.

If this Agreement or any Work Order is terminated for reasons other than material breach by Quintiles, Sponsor shall pay Quintiles for all Services properly performed in accordance with any applicable Work Order and reimburse Quintiles for all reasonable costs and expenses incurred in performing such Services, including all non-cancelable costs incurred prior to the termination date. If payments are unit or milestone based, and the Agreement or a Work Order is terminated after costs have been incurred toward achieving portions of one or more incomplete units or milestones, Sponsor will pay Quintiles’ standard fees for actual work performed toward those incomplete units or milestones up to the date of termination (not to exceed the actual amount due for completion of such milestone or unit), in addition to paying for completed units or milestones.

Upon receipt of a termination notice, Quintiles shall promptly cease performing any work not necessary for the orderly close out of the affected Project(s), or for the fulfillment of any regulatory requirements, and will submit an itemized accounting of the Services completed, expenses incurred pursuant to the performance of the Services, any non-cancelable expenses incurred relating to the unfinished Work Order, and payments received in order to determine a balance to be paid by either party to the other. Such balance will be paid within thirty (30) days of receipt of such itemized accounting.

explanation_call.reason: The fallback limb of the "control" definition — "otherwise having the ability to influence and direct the polices and direction of an entity" — contains a typographical error ("polices" for "policies") and, more materially, sets an ambiguously low threshold by coupling "influence" with "direct": influence alone does not connote control, and a court could reasonably read the disjunctive phrase to capture minority investors, significant creditors, or contractual counterparties who exert commercial influence without holding actual governing authority. This creates genuine uncertainty about which entities qualify as affiliates of either party, with direct consequences for which entities may execute Work Orders, benefit from Agreement protections, and bear obligations under the Agreement. The market-standard formulation for non-voting control is the power to direct or cause the direction of an entity's management and policies, which is both objective and consistent with established corporate law usage.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Relationship with Affiliates; Subcontracts.

Sponsor agrees that Quintiles may use the Services of its corporate affiliates to fulfill Quintiles’ obligations under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any affiliate so used shall be subject to all of the terms and conditions applicable to Quintiles under this Agreement or any Work Order, and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Quintiles under this Agreement and any Work Order. Quintiles agrees that Sponsor’s affiliates may use the services of Quintiles (and its affiliates) under this Agreement. In such event, such Sponsor’s affiliates shall be bound by all the terms and conditions of this Agreement and any Work Order and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Sponsor under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any such affiliate of Sponsor or Quintiles may execute a Work Order directly. The term “affiliate” shall mean all entities controlling, controlled by or under common control with Sponsor or Quintiles, as the case may be. The term “control” shall mean the ability to vote fifty percent (50%) or more of the voting securities of any entity or otherwise having the ability to influence and direct the polices and direction of an entity.

Quintiles shall have the right to subcontract a portion of its obligations in connection with its performance of any Project (other than to its corporate affiliates), provided that (i) Quintiles shall have obtained the prior written approval of Sponsor to the subcontract, including providing Sponsor with sufficient information to enable proper evaluation of such subcontractor; (ii) such subcontract shall not relieve Quintiles of any of its obligations under this Agreement; (iii) Quintiles shall enter into a written agreement with each subcontractor on terms and conditions consistent with this Agreement, including for the benefit of Sponsor, provisions substantially similar to those of Sections 5.0,6.0, and 11.0; (iv) each Work Order, when appropriate, shall specify the name of such subcontractors; and (v) if requested by Sponsor, Quintiles agrees to provide Sponsor with a copy of each such subcontract.

explanation_thinking_by_para.3946C9A7:
The issue identified is with the definition of "control" - specifically the phrase "otherwise having the ability to influence and direct the polices and direction of an entity." There are two problems here:

1. "polices" is a typographical error - it should be "policies"
2. The phrase "influence and direct the policies and direction of an entity" is ambiguous - "influence" is a much lower threshold than "control" and could capture relationships that shouldn't qualify as affiliates (e.g., minority investors, board observers, significant customers). Two reasonable lawyers could disagree on when "influence" alone triggers affiliate status.

The fix should be surgical - correcting the typo and tightening the alternative control definition to require actual control (not mere influence), which is market standard. The standard fallback for non-voting control is typically "the power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies of an entity."
I'll replace the flawed phrase with "otherwise having the power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies of an entity," which eliminates the overly broad "influence" standard and fixes the typo using standard market language, while leaving everything else untouched.
explanation_thinking_by_para.0D6FBDD7:
Let me analyze the issues identified:

1. **Undefined term**: "sufficient information to enable proper evaluation of such subcontractor" - "sufficient information" and "proper evaluation" are vague and undefined, leaving what constitutes adequate disclosure open to dispute.

2. **One-sided obligation without corresponding right/obligation**: Quintiles must obtain Sponsor's prior written approval, but there is no corresponding obligation on Sponsor to respond within a defined timeframe or not to unreasonably withhold approval. This could allow Sponsor to indefinitely delay or arbitrarily withhold consent, which is commercially unfair to Quintiles.

Let me draft surgical fixes:

1. Replace "sufficient information to enable proper evaluation of such subcontractor" with something more objective - e.g., "sufficient information reasonably necessary to evaluate such subcontractor"
2. Add a market-standard qualifier so Sponsor's approval right cannot be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed - changing "prior written approval of Sponsor to the subcontract" to include that parenthetical, without inventing specific time periods not already in the Agreement.

Also tightening the second clause: "sufficient information to enable proper evaluation of such subcontractor" becomes "information reasonably necessary to evaluate such subcontractor," keeping the paragraph compact while fixing both issues surgically.

suggestions.reason: The fallback limb of the "control" definition — "otherwise having the ability to influence and direct the polices and direction of an entity" — contains a typographical error ("polices" for "policies") and, more materially, sets an ambiguously low threshold by coupling "influence" with "direct": influence alone does not connote control, and a court could reasonably read the disjunctive phrase to capture minority investors, significant creditors, or contractual counterparties who exert commercial influence without holding actual governing authority. This creates genuine uncertainty about which entities qualify as affiliates of either party, with direct consequences for which entities may execute Work Orders, benefit from Agreement protections, and bear obligations under the Agreement. The market-standard formulation for non-voting control is the power to direct or cause the direction of an entity's management and policies, which is both objective and consistent with established corporate law usage.

suggestions.reason: The approval condition in proviso (i) requires Quintiles to obtain Sponsor's prior written approval before subcontracting, but imposes no corresponding obligation on Sponsor to act reasonably or within any defined period, leaving Sponsor free to withhold or delay consent arbitrarily to the commercial detriment of Quintiles and project delivery. clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Cooperation; Delays; Disclosure of Hazards.

Sponsor shall forward to Quintiles in a timely manner all documents, materials and information in Sponsor’s possession or control necessary for Quintiles to conduct the Services. Quintiles will use commercially reasonable efforts to complete the agreed upon Services within the timelines set forth in an executed Work Order or Change Order. Quintiles shall not be liable to Sponsor nor be deemed to have breached this Agreement for errors, delays or other consequences arising from Sponsor’s failure to timely provide documents, materials or information or to otherwise cooperate with Quintiles in order for Quintiles to timely and properly perform its obligations under the relevant Work Order or Change Order.

Quintiles and Sponsor agree to notify the other in writing immediately if any delays or limits are encountered in their performance of any Work Order, and shall use good faith efforts to negotiate an acceptable resolution to such delays or limits.

Sponsor shall provide Quintiles with all information available to it regarding known or potential hazards associated with the use of any substances supplied to Quintiles by Sponsor, and Sponsor shall comply with all current legislation and regulations concerning the shipment of substances by the land, sea or air. Quintiles agrees to comply with all laws, rules and regulations, including written instructions provided by Sponsor, relating to the storage and handling of any such substances received from Sponsor.

explanation_call.reason: The clause as drafted contains five material deficiencies that create bilateral commercial risk: it does not exclude events within a party's own control or caused by its own acts or omissions; it imposes no notification obligation on the affected party; it requires no mitigation or steps toward resumption of performance; it provides no termination right if the disruption persists beyond a reasonable period; and it is silent on whether continuity or recovery obligations remain in force during the excused period. Taken together, these gaps leave both parties without workable protections, could allow a party to invoke the clause for self-created disruptions, and may leave the non-affected party indefinitely bound without remedy.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Force Majeure. In the event either party is delayed or hindered in or prevented from the performance of any act required hereunder by reasons of strike, lockouts, labor troubles, inability to procure materials or services, failure of power, restrictive government or judicial orders or decrees, riots, insurrection, war, Acts of God, inclement weather, or other cause beyond that party's reasonable control and not attributable to that party's own acts or omissions, then performance of such act (except for the payment of money owed) shall be excused for the period of such delay, provided that the affected party: (a) promptly notifies the other party in writing upon the occurrence of such event; (b) uses commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate the effects of such event and to resume performance; and (c) acknowledges that any applicable business continuity or recovery obligations shall remain in effect during the period of excused performance. If such delay continues for more than sixty (60) consecutive days, either party may terminate the affected obligations upon written notice to the other party.

explanation_call.reason: The final sentence of this clause — requiring that "a currency exchange provision shall be included in the Work Order" — fails to identify which party bears the obligation to include that provision, omits any minimum content standard for what it must address, and provides no fallback mechanism if the Work Order is executed without one, leaving both parties exposed to a gap in contractual coverage for high-value multi-currency engagements exceeding $500,000. Additionally, the passive construction creates an unenforceable obligation with no identifiable obligor, meaning neither party could compel the other to satisfy it. The reimbursement mechanism in the second sentence, while commercially reasonable in direction, uses the last business Friday of the month as the conversion date without a fallback if that benchmark ceases to be published or is unavailable, creating a residual enforceability risk. These gaps are operationally significant for Work Orders involving substantial cross-currency fee exposure.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Foreign Currency Exchange. The currency to be used for invoice and payment shall be the currency stated in the Budget or Table attached to the Work Order (the "Contracted Currency"). If Quintiles incurs pass-through costs in a currency other than the Contracted Currency, then Sponsor shall reimburse Quintiles for Quintiles' actual costs in the Contracted Currency based on the Oanda foreign currency exchange rate (Oanda.com) for the applicable currencies on the last business Friday of the month in which such costs were incurred, or if such rate is unavailable, the most recently published Oanda rate prior to that date. For Work Orders that involve the performance of Services by Quintiles or its affiliates in any countries that use currencies other than the Contracted Currency, and the fees for such Services will exceed $500,000, Quintiles shall include a currency exchange provision in the applicable Work Order specifying the exchange rate mechanism, reference rate source, and applicable conversion dates; provided that if no such provision is included in the applicable Work Order, the Oanda foreign currency exchange rate mechanism set forth in this Section shall apply by default.

thinking_trace.extraction_thinking:
Let me analyze the clause carefully against each criterion.

The clause is about Foreign Currency Exchange. Let me evaluate each criterion:

**GEN-01: One-sided obligations**
The clause has some asymmetry. The obligation to reimburse Quintiles' actual costs falls on the Sponsor, using the Oanda rate on the last business Friday of the month. The Sponsor has no reciprocal protection if the currency moves unfavorably. The provision about including a currency exchange provision in Work Orders for Services exceeding $500,000 is symmetric in that it applies to both parties, but the obligation to reimburse passes through to the Sponsor. However, this is a pass-through cost reimbursement which is commercially reasonable. 

The $500,000 threshold for requiring a currency exchange provision applies to both parties' Services, which is symmetric. But the actual reimbursement obligation sits on the Sponsor without any corresponding protection if rates swing in Quintiles' favor, making this a pass-through arrangement that leans one-sided but is fairly standard for cost reimbursement clauses.

Moving to time standards, the clause specifies "the last business Friday of the month," which is a definite marker rather than a vague phrase like "promptly," so that criterion is met. The financial elements—the $500,000 threshold, the determinable Oanda rate, and the Contracted Currency defined by reference to the Work Order—are all sufficiently specific, satisfying that requirement too.

On undefined terms, I'm noting that "Budget," "Table," and "pass-through costs" aren't formally defined but carry plain commercial meaning, while "Contracted Currency" is defined within the clause itself—though "currency exchange provision" in the final sentence remains ambiguous as to what it actually refers to.

Checking the remaining criteria: no unlimited liability is created since reimbursement is tied to actual costs, no unfilled placeholders exist, and there are no contradictions with other visible provisions. However, I'm flagging an unpaired obligation issue—the requirement that a "currency exchange provision" be included in large foreign-currency Work Orders doesn't specify who must include it or what it should contain, and similarly, the Sponsor must reimburse pass-through costs while Quintiles bears no corresponding duty to hedge or mitigate exchange rate exposure.

I'm also noting ambiguity around what exactly the currency exchange provision needs to contain, plus an unclear precedence between the "Budget" and "Table" if both are attached to a Work Order. On conditions and triggers, the clause is fairly clear: the currency provision requirement triggers at $500,000 in fees for services performed in non-contracted currencies, and the reimbursement obligation triggers whenever Quintiles incurs pass-through costs in another currency.

Reconsidering GEN-01, while the rate-setting mechanism is standard, the Sponsor has no way to verify or dispute costs and bears all FX risk alone, so I'm settling on "Partly met" rather than fully met. Similarly for GEN-08, the obligation to include a currency exchange provision lacks detail on who proposes it, what it must contain, or what happens absent agreement -- another "Partly met."

Let me analyze the issues identified in this clause:

The phrase "a currency exchange provision shall be included in the Work Order" is vague and unenforceable - it doesn't specify what that provision must contain, who is responsible for including it, what happens if it's not included, or what the default mechanism is if the Work Order lacks such a provision.

3. The obligation to include a currency exchange provision in the Work Order is passive/unnamed - it doesn't identify which party bears the obligation to include it.
4. I also want to flag that the pass-through reimbursement is somewhat one-sided toward Quintiles, though that's fairly standard commercial practice since it covers actual costs incurred. I'll keep the first two sentences intact since the Oanda mechanism is commercially reasonable, and just revise the last sentence to name Quintiles as responsible for including the provision and specify what happens if it's omitted.

My redraft requires Quintiles to specify the exchange rate mechanism, source, and conversion dates in the Work Order when applicable, with the Oanda rate applying by default if no such provision exists. explanation_call.reason: The clause grants Quintiles an uncapped, unilateral right to increase fees each calendar year without any advance notice obligation, leaving the other party with no meaningful opportunity to plan for or contest the increase. The selection mechanism for the benchmark rate is ambiguous: the use of "or" between the four percent (4%) floor and the Economist wages/earnings survey index does not specify whether Quintiles selects at its discretion or whether the higher or lower figure governs, which two reasonable lawyers would read differently. Additionally, "equivalent inflation index of the country where services are performed" is undefined and not anchored to any objective publication or governmental source, creating a material dispute risk wherever multi-country services are involved.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Inflation Adjustments. Where services in a Work Order are provided by Quintiles over multiple calendar years, Quintiles may increase its fees at the beginning of each calendar year to reflect increases in Quintiles' business costs on a prospective basis only, provided that Quintiles delivers written notice of any such increase to the other party no less than sixty (60) days prior to the start of the applicable calendar year. Quintiles' overall costs may be increased for the next twelve (12) month period using the lesser of four percent (4%) or the average percentage change in the wages/earnings survey as published in the Economist (or as reported at www.economist.com), or, where services are performed outside the United States, the lesser of four percent (4%) or the equivalent nationally recognized government-published wage or consumer price index for the country where services are performed, over the preceding twelve (12) month period.

explanation_thinking_by_para.690FFE25:
Let me analyze the issues identified in this clause:

1. **One-sided obligation**: Only Quintiles may increase fees; there's no corresponding right for the other party (Customer/Client) to benefit from cost decreases or to contest increases.

2. **Undefined terms**: "equivalent inflation index of the country where services are performed" is not defined and leaves which index applies open to dispute.

3. **Unilateral right without corresponding obligation**: Quintiles "may" increase fees but has no obligation to notify the other party in advance, and there's no cap or floor mechanism protecting the Customer.

4. **Ambiguity in operative effect**: The clause uses "four percent (4%) or the average percentage change in the wages/earnings survey" - it's unclear whether this means the higher of the two, the lower of the two, or Quintiles' choice. The word "or" creates ambiguity about how the index is selected and by whom.


For a balanced fix, I should resolve the "or" ambiguity by specifying the lower of the two benchmarks rather than leaving the choice open, since that's the market-standard approach and protects the Customer while keeping things fair to Quintiles. I also want to address the undefined inflation index by adding a fallback definition, and consider whether an advance notice requirement should be added.

I'm also weighing whether this clause should be bilateral, letting fees adjust downward too if underlying costs decrease, though the priority is to keep my edits surgical and close to the original word count rather than rewriting the whole provision. Now I'm drafting the revised language for the inflation adjustment clause.

explanation_call.reason: The assignment clause as drafted contains several material gaps that create commercial and legal risk for both parties equally. It imposes an absolute consent requirement with no stated standard, no response deadline, and no carve-out for routine affiliate transfers or business succession events such as mergers or asset sales, meaning either party could unreasonably block an ordinary corporate reorganization. The clause is also silent on the transferring party's continuing liability post-assignment, on the obligation to notify the non-assigning party of a permitted transfer, and on the treatment of a change of control — leaving neither party with a clear contractual right to respond to a de facto assignment by acquisition. These gaps expose both Sponsor and Quintiles to uncertainty regarding the enforceability of assignments and the identity of the contracting counterparty over the Agreement's term.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Binding Agreement and Assignment. This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of Sponsor and Quintiles and their respective successors and permitted assigns. Except as stated above in Section 17.1, neither party may assign any of its rights or obligations under this Agreement without the other party's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, and to be provided within thirty (30) days of a written request; provided that either party may assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, upon prior written notice to the non-assigning party. The assigning party shall remain liable for its obligations under this Agreement unless expressly released in writing by the other party. A change of control of either party shall constitute an assignment requiring consent under this Section.

clause_units.clause_title: Choice of Law, Waiver and Enforceability

failed_criteria.question: Is a waiver effective only if it is in writing and signed by the waiving party?

explanation_call.reason: The waiver provision states that failure to enforce a right does not constitute a waiver and that waiving one breach does not waive subsequent breaches, but it does not require that any effective waiver be in writing and signed by the waiving party. Without this requirement, either party risks having a waiver implied from conduct, oral representations, or a course of dealing, which creates genuine uncertainty about the enforceability of contractual rights on both sides. This is a material gap against market-standard drafting for a Master Services Agreement, as an unsigned or oral waiver could later be asserted to have modified substantive rights or remedies. No cross-reference or survival alignment issues arise from this amendment.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Choice of Law, Waiver and Enforceability. This Agreement shall be construed, governed, interpreted, and applied in accordance with the laws of the State of New York exclusive of its conflicts of law provisions. The failure to enforce any right or provision herein shall not constitute a waiver of that right or provision. No waiver of any right or provision shall be effective unless made in writing and signed by the waiving party. Any waiver of a breach of a provision shall not constitute a waiver of any subsequent breach of that provision. If any provisions herein are found to be unenforceable on the grounds that they are overly broad or in conflict with applicable laws, it is the intent of the parties that such provisions be replaced, reformed or narrowed so that their original business purpose can be accomplished to the extent permitted by law, and that the remaining provisions shall not in any way be affected or impaired thereby.
