explanation_call.reason: The arbitration clause omits five material elements that together create significant enforceability and operational risk for both parties: it does not state the governing law, it identifies only the filing location rather than formally designating a seat of arbitration, it contains no pre-arbitration escalation step or timeframe, it does not preserve either party's right to seek interim court relief for urgent matters such as injunctive relief, and it is silent on each party's obligation to continue performing during a pending dispute. Without a governing law designation, courts may face uncertainty in interpreting the agreement's substantive terms, while the absence of a formal seat creates jurisdictional ambiguity over supervisory court proceedings. The lack of a continuity-of-performance obligation during disputes creates commercial risk for both parties, particularly where Services under the Agreement are time-sensitive.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Arbitration. Prior to initiating arbitration, the parties shall attempt to resolve any dispute through good-faith senior executive negotiation for thirty (30) days following written notice of the dispute. Any unresolved controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement or the breach thereof shall be settled by binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association ("AAA") under its Commercial Arbitration Rules and the Federal Arbitration Act, and judgment on the award rendered by the arbitrator shall be binding and may be entered in any court having jurisdiction thereof. Such arbitration shall be filed and conducted at the AAA office closest to the Quintiles office having responsibility for the Project, which location shall constitute the seat of arbitration, and shall be conducted in English by one arbitrator mutually acceptable to the parties selected in accordance with AAA Rules. The arbitrator shall not have the power to award punitive damages or any damages excluded by this Agreement. Either party may seek interim or provisional court relief without waiving its right to arbitration, and each party shall continue performing its obligations under this Agreement pending resolution of any dispute.

explanation_call.reason: An entire agreement clause that contains no carve-out for fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation creates a risk that a party could argue the clause bars claims arising from pre-contractual fraudulent inducement, since the clause supersedes all prior agreements, negotiations, and discussions without qualification. Market-standard drafting requires an explicit statement that nothing in the entire agreement clause excludes or limits either party's liability for fraud, preserving that cause of action for both parties equally. Without this carve-out, the clause is commercially one-sided in favor of a wrongdoing party and may be unenforceable in whole or in part under applicable law if a court construes the supersession language as an attempted exclusion of fraud liability.

explanation_call.reason: The clause identifies the Work Order and the Master Agreement as the operative documents but does not expressly establish a priority rule between them in the event of conflict, leaving it uncertain which document governs where they diverge. Without an explicit statement that the Master Agreement prevails, a party could argue that the more specific or later-dated Work Order overrides the Master Agreement on any point it touches. Additionally, the clause contains no exclusion of extraneous terms, such as a party's standard terms, purchase orders, or online terms, leaving the door open to unintended incorporation of outside documents that could displace negotiated Master Agreement protections.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Work Order. This document constitutes a "Work Order" under the Master Agreement, and this Work Order and the services contemplated herein are subject to the terms and provisions of the Master Agreement, which shall prevail in the event of any conflict with this Work Order. No other terms (including either party's standard terms or purchase orders) shall form part of or be incorporated into the agreement between the parties.

explanation_call.reason: The clause as drafted contains no operative payment mechanics whatsoever — it lists only attachment references, leaving fees, invoicing, payment timing, fee variability, invoice disputes, late-payment consequences, and expense treatment entirely unstated in the body of the Agreement. This creates material enforceability risk for both parties: the Service Provider has no enforceable payment right on the face of the Agreement, and the Customer has no contractual basis on which to dispute an invoice, withhold a contested amount, or challenge an expense charge. Because all substantive commercial payment terms are deferred exclusively to Attachments without any fallback standard in the main body, any gap, ambiguity, or conflict within those Attachments leaves both parties without a contractual safety net.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: The following Attachments form part of this Agreement and together govern the commercial terms between the parties: SCOPE OF WORK – ATTACHMENT 1; PROJECT BUDGET – ATTACHMENT 2; TIMELINE – ATTACHMENT 3; PAYMENT SCHEDULE – ATTACHMENT 4; TRANSFER OF OBLIGATIONS (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 5; LOCAL REPRESENTATIVE DUTIES (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 6. Fees shall be calculated as set forth in Attachment 2 and invoiced in accordance with Attachment 4; where Attachment 4 does not specify a frequency, invoices shall be issued monthly in arrears. All undisputed invoices are due within thirty (30) days of receipt. Either party may dispute an invoice in writing within fifteen (15) days of receipt, specifying the basis for dispute; undisputed amounts remain due by the original payment date. Late payments on undisputed amounts accrue interest at the lesser of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law. Fees are fixed as set out in Attachment 2 and may not be varied except by written amendment signed by both parties. Out-of-pocket expenses are either included within Attachment 2 or, if not so included, require prior written approval from the other party before being incurred.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Services and Payment of Fees and Expenses. The specific services contemplated by this Work Order (the “Services”) and the related payment terms and obligations are set forth on the following attachments, which are incorporated herein by reference:

SCOPE OF WORK – ATTACHMENT 1; PROJECT BUDGET – ATTACHMENT 2; TIMELINE – ATTACHMENT 3; PAYMENT SCHEDULE – ATTACHMENT 4; TRANSFER OF OBLIGATIONS (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 5; LOCAL REPRESENTATIVE DUTIES (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 6

To the extent that any terms and provisions in any of the attachments hereto conflict with the Master Agreement and this Work Order, the terms and provisions of the Master Agreement and this Task Order shall control.

explanation_call.reason: The Term clause defers all termination mechanics entirely to the Master Agreement without incorporating any self-contained provisions for termination grounds, cure periods, notice requirements, written form, effective date of termination, post-termination consequences, or survival of obligations. This creates material operational uncertainty for both parties: neither party can determine from the Work Order alone on what grounds or how it may exit, what notice is required, or what financial and practical obligations follow. The continuation provision governing the scenario where the Master Agreement lapses while the Work Order remains open also fails to address which specific provisions are intended to survive, which could expose either party to unintended ongoing obligations or the loss of critical protections.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Term. The term of this Work Order shall commence on the date of execution and shall continue until the services described in Attachment 1 are completed, unless earlier terminated by either party: (i) for the other party's material breach, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice if such breach remains uncured at the end of that period; (ii) for convenience, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice; or (iii) otherwise in accordance with the Master Agreement. Termination takes effect upon expiry of the applicable notice period. Upon termination, all undisputed fees for work performed through the effective date of termination shall be paid, prepaid amounts for unperformed services shall be refunded, and each party shall promptly return the other's materials. Confidentiality, payment, and liability provisions shall survive termination. If the Master Agreement is terminated or expires but this Work Order is not terminated or completed, the terms of the Master Agreement shall continue to apply to this Work Order until the Work Order is either terminated or completed.

If the Master Agreement is terminated or expires, but this Work Order is not terminated or completed, then the terms of the Master Agreement shall continue to apply to this Work Order until the Work Order is either terminated or completed.

suggestions.reason: The clause expressly binds corporate affiliates to all terms and conditions of the Master Agreement and Work Order, but imposes no equivalent obligation on non-affiliate subcontractors and consultants: they are merely listed, with no requirement that they be bound by materially equivalent obligations, including confidentiality, data protection, or security. This gap means that third-party subcontractors performing material portions of the Services could operate outside the contractual framework that governs Quintiles itself, creating meaningful exposure for both parties. Where subcontractors handle sensitive data or Confidential Information, the absence of a downstream binding obligation undermines the protections established elsewhere in the Master Agreement.

suggestions.suggested_fix: Affiliates and Subcontractors. Sponsor agrees that Quintiles may use the services of its corporate affiliates to fulfill Quintiles' obligations under this Work Order. Any such affiliates shall be bound by all the terms and conditions of, and be entitled to all rights and protections afforded under, the Master Agreement and this Work Order. Any subcontractors or consultants (other than Quintiles' affiliates) that will be used by Quintiles in performing the Services are listed below, and Quintiles shall ensure that each such subcontractor or consultant is bound by written obligations materially equivalent to those imposed on Quintiles under the Master Agreement and this Work Order, including with respect to confidentiality, data protection, and security. Quintiles shall remain liable for the acts and omissions of its subcontractors and consultants to the same extent as if performed by Quintiles directly.

suggestions.reason: The clause identifies a list of approved subcontractors and consultants but contains only an unfilled placeholder, leaving three material gaps: it does not establish whether the other party must consent to or be notified of additions or substitutions, it imposes no ongoing responsibility on Quintiles for its subcontractors' acts or omissions, and it provides no mechanism for the other party to object to changes. Without a retained-responsibility provision, Quintiles could disclaim liability for subcontractor failures, while without a consent or notice mechanism, the other party has no practical ability to protect itself against undisclosed substitutions. These omissions create material enforceability and accountability risks for both parties across the term of the Agreement.

explanation_call.reason: The Currency Exchange clause contains no operative contractual language whatsoever; it is an unfilled drafting instruction enclosed in brackets, rendering the provision entirely unenforceable and without legal effect. Because the clause is triggered in Work Orders where fees or expenses exceed one million US Dollars in a foreign currency, the absence of any agreed conversion mechanism, reference rate, or rate determination date creates material financial uncertainty for both parties on significant cross-currency transactions. No court could determine the rights or obligations of either party from this text, and the gap could give rise to disputed payment calculations or unresolved currency exposure in every affected Work Order.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Currency Exchange. Where Quintiles earns fees or incurs expenses in excess of one million US Dollars (USD 1,000,000) under a Work Order in a currency other than the invoice and payment currency, such amounts shall be converted to the invoice and payment currency at the mid-market exchange rate published by the European Central Bank on the last Business Day of the calendar month in which such fees are earned or expenses are incurred.

explanation_call.reason: The Inflation and Cost Adjustment clause consists entirely of an unfilled placeholder and contains no operative text, meaning it creates no enforceable rights or obligations for either party on the commercially significant issue of fee adjustments over time. As drafted, neither party has a defined mechanism, index, cap, notice period, or recourse right, leaving the economic terms of any long-term engagement entirely open to dispute. This omission exposes both parties to uncertainty: the service provider has no contractual basis to pass through cost increases, while the customer has no protection against uncapped or unilateral price changes. The clause must be replaced with a complete, bilaterally balanced operative provision before execution.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Inflation and Cost Adjustment. Either party may request an adjustment to the Fees once per calendar year upon no less than sixty (60) days' prior written notice to the other party. Any such adjustment shall not exceed the percentage change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) published by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics for the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the date of such notice. If the parties fail to agree on an adjusted Fee schedule within thirty (30) days following such notice, either party may terminate the affected Order Form upon no less than thirty (30) days' written notice, without liability to the other party solely by reason of such termination.
